P1.evidence: Setter acknowledged with nothing read back — 'he kind of gave me a little bit of a background.' Frame was two-part plus alignment: 'I just want to get a good idea where you're at... really build out what it is you want to accomplish, and then [if] there's alignment, we can talk about the coaching.' No what's-in-the-way, no what-you-need, and no agreement question. Open question ran verbatim.

P2.evidence: Training history, diet and energy were all covered properly and in detail — the rowing week was reconstructed session by session, and the vegetarian diet was explored down to protein sources. Everything else was skipped. No age, no height, no weight. No occupation, despite the prospect saying twice that a job change and longer commute were what ended his training — the rep never asked what the job is. No health conditions, no injuries, no movement limitations, nothing hereditary. Sleep was volunteered inside the energy answer ('I do get my eight hours of sleep') rather than asked. This prospect finished the call as an almost entirely unknown quantity.

P3.evidence: The best move on the call was the look-versus-feel fork: 'is it more so about how you feel, or is it more so like how you look for you?' answered 'How I feel, I think', followed by 'How do you want to feel?' That is exactly the right question. The prospect gave a thin answer — 'more capable of what I was able to do' — and the rep accepted it and moved on rather than pressing. The bridge to what is actually driving it was never asked, nobody else's stake was ever raised, and nothing was driven through to identity or longevity. The reflect-back stayed descriptive: 'it's like a little bit discouraging... I used to be up here doing all of this. And now when I go to the gym, I can't do as much.'

P4.evidence: The strongest phase of the call. Past training was mapped thoroughly and the falling-off was traced properly — 'you said your training kind of tapered off, right?' and 'How long ago was it that you moved and that all changed?' — establishing a ten-month decline caused by a move, a job change, a longer commute and loss of rowing access. What was missing is the structural reframe: the prospect's own diagnosis is time scarcity and lost rhythm, and the rep never tested it, never asked why it did not stick, and never ran 'the information isn't the problem, why can't you stick to it on your own?' That mattered here, because the product he was then steered toward is self-guided and solves none of what he described.

P5.evidence: Never ran in any form. The prospect had supplied the raw material — 'I can see myself losing a bit of that' — and no consequence question followed.

P6.evidence: No commitment check of any kind. The call went from 'That makes sense, dude' at 00:12:16 directly into 'I do have something in mind for you... I'll tell you the numbers for both.' No belief question, no all-in question, and no yes of any sort was obtained before the price was named.

P11.evidence: Scored rather than marked not applicable, because the call did reach the offer — two prices were named and a product was demonstrated on screen for five minutes. No attempt was made to collect payment, no onboarding call with Trevor was mentioned, no agreement, no welcome email, no questionnaire. The rep ended on 'if you want to do it, do it. If you don't, don't.'

objection_plays.detail: 'I'll have a think, and then would I get back to you' is a textbook OA trigger and not one move ran. No 'do you feel what we've gone through CAN get you to your goal', no 'what makes you feel it can', no 'what's actually coming up that's preventing you from getting started', no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is.' The rep's response was to hand over the decision entirely: 'I'll just text you the link over, and if you want to do it, do it. If you don't, don't.'

Script gap, and the decisive event of the call. The rep created a price fork himself — £4,400 for six months of coaching against £150 a month self-guided — and asked 'Which one would you want to take a look at?' The prospect answered 'Self-guided, please' in under two seconds. No budget had been established, no objection had been raised, and the coaching was never presented, justified or re-offered. The playbook has no guidance on when a low-tier product may be introduced or how to sell against it, so the rep anchored the company's own premium offer against the company's own cheap one and lost the coaching sale without a single objection being spoken.

notes: The process effectively stopped at the twelve-minute mark: discovery was decent on training and diet, then the rep skipped the philosophy presentation, the consequence frame and the commitment check and went straight to naming two prices. Two things to coach directly — never present the self-guided tier alongside the coaching as a menu, and get the monthly arithmetic right, because £4,400 over six months was quoted here as £880 a month against a correct £733 on another call the same day.
